techTree.title: Tech tree
techTree.intro: Every building, and what each of its ten levels costs, produces, and requires.

lore.longhouse: The heart of the settlement. Its level sets claim radius, build slots and how many settlers call the village home — every settlement starts with one, standing on grass.
lore.lumberjack: Fells timber on forested ground — the wood behind every wall and roof.
lore.quarry: Cuts stone from a mountain ridge — the bones of every keep.
lore.farm: Grows food on open grassland, keeping the longhouse table full.
lore.storagehouse: Extra room for the harvest on grass, so a full warehouse never stalls production.
lore.tower: A watch built on grass or sand at the border, pushing the claimed ground further out.
lore.fishinghut: A dock over shallow water, fishing the shallows a farm never could.
lore.magictower: Arcane iron out of grassland — no ore, no vein, just the working.
lore.pumpkinfarm: A second harvest for grass — pumpkins alongside the plain fields.
lore.shrineofthor: Raised to Thor on grass — its favour boosts Wood and Stone production.
lore.shrineoffreyja: Raised to Freyja on grass — its favour boosts Food production.
lore.shrineofullr: Raised to Ullr on grass — its favour boosts Wood production.
lore.shrineofnjord: Raised to Njörd on grass — its favour boosts storage capacity rather than any resource's production.
lore.archeryrange: Trains the land army — spearmen through catapults — on grass or sand, in place of the longhouse.
lore.dockyard: Trains ships on shallow (coastal) water, in place of the longhouse.
lore.greatstorehouse: A late-game storage tier on grass, needing both the longhouse and this settlement's own storage house at level 10.
lore.barracks: A garrison raised on grass or sand at the border.
lore.fisherhut: A second dock for the table, working grassland like a farm rather than the shallows.
lore.sawmill: Refines timber on grass, alongside a neighbouring Lumberjack — its look changes when built next to a river or a river bend.

tiles.title: Tiles
tiles.intro: The terrain a world is made of, how it generates, and what can be built on it.
tiles.movementRiverNote: Land armies pay a one-time crossing penalty of {cost} extra hex-equivalents entering a river tile, on top of the terrain underneath it. Ships never cross rivers.
tiles.riverSawmillNote: The Sawmill is the one building that goes directly on a river tile — only a Straight or Bend one.

sea.title: Sea
sea.lore: Open water. Nothing stands on it, and nothing is grown or mined here — it only ever separates islands.
sea.generation: Every hex outside an island's radius.

coastalWater.title: Coastal water
coastalWater.lore: Still plain sea underneath — the same terrain as the open water beyond it — but close enough to the shore for a dock.
coastalWater.generation: A sea hex with at least one land neighbour: the ring hugging every island.

sand.title: Sand
sand.lore: An island's beach — the coastal ring settlers actually land on when founding a settlement.
sand.generation: The outer edge of an island: beyond 82% of its radius from centre.

grass.title: Grass
grass.lore: Open lowland — most of a settlement is built here.
grass.generation: Lowland too smooth to be forest and too far from the centre to be mountain.

forest.title: Forest
forest.lore: Lowland gone rocky enough to grow trees instead of open grass.
forest.generation: Rockiness above the forest threshold, but not steep enough for mountain.

mountain.title: Mountain
mountain.lore: The rockiest ground an island has.
mountain.generation: Confined to an island's interior (within 40% of its radius) so ridges never form on the coast.

river.title: River
river.lore: Water cut through the land itself, from a mountain spring down to the sea — a river tile's art fully replaces whatever land terrain it flows over.
river.generation: Traced downhill from a spring on a qualifying mountain cluster (2+ connected mountain tiles) to the coast, meandering as it goes; two rivers that cross merge into a confluence, and anything shorter than 2 tiles is discarded.
